subject: "Error: The following items have only one response category and cannot be estimated"

messages.author: 1781f73f3258f999
messages.subject: "Error: The following items have only one response category and cannot be estimated"
parts:
I'm trying to obtain the fit of a model in one sample based on estimates from another sample. So, something like this:

mirt.out1 <- mirt(data = sample1.dat, model=2, method="EM")


parvals1 <- mod2values(mirt.out1)


mirt.out2 <- mirt(data = sample2.dat, model=2, pars=parvals1, TOL=NaN)


However, when I do that, I receive the error message "Error: The following items have only one response category and cannot be estimated", because one item in the second sample has no variation.

I can understand why the error might be thrown in estimating a model, but in my case, I'm just trying to get the fit of the model at specific parameter estimate values.

Is there a way to do this without removing the offending item? I thought about multiple group options, but don't want to jointly estimate parameters; I want to estimate parameters in one sample, and then calculate the fit of those parameters in a second sample.

Thanks.

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: "Error: The following items have only one response category and cannot be estimated"
parts:
It's possible to trick the second model into thinking there are more categories than what was observed by passing a customK argument to the technical list. If you extract the K vector from the original model via extract.mirt(mirt.out1, 'K') and use this in the definition for the second model it should work fine. I believe someone recently asked a similar question about cross validation with mirt(), so if you search the forum you should be able to find the thread. HTH.

Phil

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: "Error: The following items have only one response category and cannot be estimated"
parts:
Can you provide a reproducible example? The following worked fine for me:

---------------
library(mirt)
sample1.dat <- expand.table(LSAT7)
sample2.dat <- sample1.dat[1:10,]

mirt.out1 <- mirt(data = sample1.dat, model=1, method="EM")

parvals1 <- mod2values(mirt.out1)

mirt.out2 <- mirt(data = sample2.dat, model=1, pars=parvals1, TOL=NaN,
                  technical = list(customK=rep(2, 5)))
mirt.out1
mirt.out2
coef(mirt.out1, simplify=TRUE)
coef(mirt.out2, simplify=TRUE)
---------------  

Phil

messages.author: 1781f73f3258f999
messages.subject: Re: "Error: The following items have only one response category and cannot be estimated"
parts: Sorry -- I figured it out. There was a call to M2() which I didn't notice; this was causing the error. Running M2(mirt.out2, calcNull=F) seems to fix it.
